The figure above shows the graph of a piecewise linear function $y=f(x).$ The point $A$ has coordinates $(1,1)$ and lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $(1,1)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x),$ what is $({f}^{-1})^{′}(1)?$

feedback.worked_solution:
Since $(1,1)$ lies on ${f}^{-1},$ we have ${f}^{-1}(1)=1.$ 
The slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ for $x\in [-2,4]$ is $\frac{2}{3}$, hence, ${f}^{′}(1)=\frac{2}{3}.$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse function is 

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Evaluating at $x=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
